offer.say: So they named an award after me. The Pruett. Most improved. And I'm looking in the lost and found for my glove, and there's a trophy. MOST IMPROVED 1991. Nobody's claimed it in thirty-five years. That's my people, {owner}. That's a fellow improver. I need to know who.

options.text: Why does it matter to you?
Did you just stop in front of me on purpose?

why.say: Because improving is lonely. Everybody claps for the good ones. Nobody claps for the guy who stood up. I want to clap for the guy who stood up in 1991.

cheek.say: Every opportunity. Every single one. It never gets old. Will you help me?

options.text: Yes. Stop stopping and let's look.

decline.say: Everything's somebody's. That's what lost and found means. It's found. It's just waiting.

accepted.say: It's in the crate. Under the retainer. Don't touch the retainer.

options.text: I'll get the trophy out of the crate.
Asking Midge to check the archive.
I have a name. I want to ask her first.

p_doreen.say: Her? A her! A fellow improver! Is she still skating? Please say she's still skating.

complete.say: Doreen? DOREEN? Organ 2 Doreen? She couldn't stand in January 1991? She runs the clock! She's the most terrifying person in the building! And she improved! I'm... I need to sit down. I'm going to stop first.

options.text: She wants you to have it.
It belongs in the trophy case, next to the Last Call Cup.

c_gary.say: Me? I'll put it on the Wobbly Pops bench. Every game. For the improvers. Doreen's going to play the dirge at me, isn't she. Worth it.

c_case.say: With a label. 'Most Improved 1991, Mrs D. Vachon. Claimed 2026.' And under it, smaller: 'Found by G. Pruett.' Smaller. I'm humble.

c_thank.say: I'm going to stop right in front of her timekeeper's box and say thank you. She's going to hate it. She's going to love it.

done.say: Improvers, unite. Slowly. With good stops.
